Olá, somos os  SpaceDevz!

Somos uma equipe apaixonada por Tecnologias, Buscamos unir criatividade e rigor científico para transformar ideias inovadoras em soluções reais. Nosso foco está em unir diferentes perspectivas para criar um projeto memorável e de alto impacto para o desafio.

Queremos construir uma solução divertida sobre a exploração espacial!
summary: OrbitCraft is an interactive 2D isometric space mission simulation game where players collaborate in real time as Flight Commander, Systems Engineer, Logistics Officer, or Communications Specialist—to design, build, test, and pilot the Icarus-1 probe to Mars within a strict 20-minute launch window, balancing authentic aerospace trade-offs validated by NASA's GMAT and systems engineering standards.
details:
The Challenge

Designing and executing an interplanetary space mission demands continuous evaluation of conflicting trade-offs: scientific return, structural mass, solar flux decline, battery depth-of-discharge during eclipses, communication link margins, launch deadlines, and strict financial budgets. For students and enthusiasts, these real-world constraints rarely exist in one unified, hands-on experience.

What is OrbitCraft?

Developed by team SpaceDevz for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, OrbitCraft is an educational web simulation game set in the illustrated 2D isometric Icarus Space Center. Players step through the complete, uncompressed lifecycle of an aerospace mission in ~20 minutes:

1. Briefing: Flight Director Dr. Helena Vaz delivers the mission directive the transfer window to Mars opens now and permanently closes in 20 minutes.

2. Modular Spacecraft Design (CAD): The Systems Engineer selects a base platform (Compact S, Interplanetary M, or Heavy L) and configures 6 subsystem slots (Propulsion, Propellant Tanks, Power, Communications, Avionics, and Scientific Payload). The game continuously evaluates 4 critical engineering requirements:

- Available Delta-V: ≥ 3,600 m/s (via Tsiolkovsky Rocket Equation).

- Mars Solar Power: Generated power ≥ consumed power (accounting for the 57% solar irradiance drop at 1.52 AU).

- Radio Link Margin: ≥ 3 dB with ground stations.

- Wet Mass: ≤ 5,000 kg launcher payload capacity.

3. Procurement & Supply Chain: Logistics orders hardware across 3 distinct suppliers (OrbiTech: space-qualified and reliable but expensive; Astra: balanced; BaraTec: cheap surplus with high manufacturing defect rates).

4. Assembly: Players physically carry delivered crates from the receiving dock across the facility to the bay (with heavy propulsion crates requiring two-person collaborative lifting).

5. Testing & Diagnostics: In the Test Bench, each subsystem undergoes NASA CubeSat 101 qualification runs (TVAC thermal vacuum and vibration stress). Defective units must be repaired in the bay or scrapped and re-ordered.

6. Launch Clearance & Board Verification: Communications calibrates the ground antenna dish, uploads navigation plans, and the crew completes four subsystem operational checkouts before the Commander issues the final GO / NO-GO decision.

7. 2D Flight & Orbital Capture: The Commander pilots the probe through interplanetary space with the exact physical Delta-V built into the craft, managing drift while Communications maintains telemetry links from Earth.

8. Evaluation: Comprehensive post-mission scorecard across 6 dimensions: Conformance to Design, Budget Efficiency, Build Quality, Punctuality, Flight Precision, and Subsystem Health.

 Gameplay Modes

- Single Player (Autonomous AI Crew): The player commands the mission while three fully autonomous NPCs (Eng. Rui Lopes, Logistics Officer Mr. Matias, and Comms Operator Sofia Neves) navigate the map using pathfinding, carry crates, and report anomalies.

- Multiplayer (LAN & Online WebSockets): Up to 4 human players collaborate in real time with spatial audio and integrated WebRTC voice communications.
